extra_snippets: And Naïve has scaled annual run-rate revenue by 10x to the low double-digit millions over the past six months, CEO and co-founder Sean Dorje said. ... Based on that traction, the company has now raised $28.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.

So I wasn’t very surprised to hear that Naïve, which offers infrastructure that lets AI agents take on the bulk of the work involved in running a business, had signed up over 30,000 developer customers within months of its launch.

It packages the process of assembling payments, email accounts, phone numbers, cloud infrastructure, storage, and company incorporation behind a single API. Naïve supplies a prompt that developers can provide to tools like Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex, which can connect to the company’s API to provision the infrastructure to set up a business.

It’s building a model router to send queries to the most efficient model for a task while preserving and replaying already reasoned data; a memory system that stores and surfaces business context as needed by agents to do their tasks; and an orchestrator for dividing work among agents. Notably, Naïve is also building a serverless runtime that runs agents within lightweight JavaScript environments rather than assigning each one a complete virtual machine — an approach that lets customers pay primarily when an agent is active and makes it less expensive to deploy large numbers of agents.

Naïve has raised $28.5 million in a Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners, with Y Combinator, Zetta Venture Partners and Liquid 2 Ventures also taking part. The round comes about nine months after the company's $2 million seed and takes disclosed funding to $30.5 million. The company sells the plumbing an AI agent needs before it can do anything consequential.

Naïve was founded in 2025 by chief executive Sean Dorje and chief technology officer Dennis Zax, went through Y Combinator's Spring 2025 batch, and is based in San Francisco with a team still in the low tens. The investor list leans toward funds that write early cheques into developer infrastructure, and Nexus leading at this size implies the round was priced on the pace of adoption rather than revenue.

Nine months and a fourteen-fold step up in round size is the cadence of a market pricing scarcity, not of a company that has settled its unit economics. extra_snippets: AI infrastructure startup Naïve has raised $28.5 million in Series A funding as it looks to make it easier for developers to build businesses that are operated, at least partly, by AI agents. The round was led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from Y Combinator, Zetta, Liquid 2 and angel investors including Gokul Rajaram, Apollo.io co-founder Tim Zheng and former HubSpot COO JD Sherman.

The latest investment takes Naïve’s total funding to roughly $32 million. The startup is targeting an increasingly obvious problem in the agentic AI market: AI can generate software and perform tasks, but actually turning that software into an operational company still requires dozens of services, accounts, payment systems and administrative processes. Naïve says it has attracted more than 30,000 developer customers within months of launching.

Naïve essentially provides a common infrastructure layer that AI agents can use to handle tasks normally spread across multiple business services. Its platform can help provision email accounts, phone numbers, virtual cards, databases, cloud computing resources and storage.

The company's website says its platform now supports connections with 100+ third-party tools and offers model routing across 300+ AI models. One of Naïve's more unusual features is company incorporation.
